\ednentry{
  id = {EDN-64},
  title = {Pynblint runs from a locked environment behind a wrapper},
  note = {\textbf{Absorbs EDN-65} (2026-10-01): which Pynblint rules are enforced.},
  date = {2026-10-01},
  milestone = {M3: Quality Assurance},
  topic = {Static Analysis, CI/CD},
  participants = {@lukas2510},
  decision = {Pynblint 0.1.6 runs from its own locked environment in \texttt{tools/\allowbreak{}pynblint-\allowbreak{}env/\allowbreak{}}.
The wrapper \texttt{tools/\allowbreak{}notebook\_\allowbreak{}lint.\allowbreak{}py} reads Pynblint's JSON report and fails the build, in \texttt{make notebook-\allowbreak{}lint} and in CI.
The table on the Notebooks page lists every rule as enforced or excluded with its reason, and the wrapper reads that table as its configuration.
The rules that read execution counts are excluded, because nbstripout removes the counts.},
  rationale = {\emph{Alternatives considered:}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, topsep=2pt]
\item \texttt{uvx pynblint}, as the issue proposed: its transitive dependencies float, and a new click release crashed the tool.
\item Pynblint alone as the CI step: it exits 0 whatever it finds.
\item \texttt{nbstripout -\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}keep-\allowbreak{}count}, so the execution rules can fire: the counts churn in every diff and do not show that a fresh kernel runs the notebook.
\end{itemize}
\par
\emph{Why:} Three measured facts about Pynblint decided how to run it: it breaks on an unpinned dependency, it exits 0 with findings, and environment variables reconfigure it.
A rule is enforced where it can fire on a committed notebook and excluded where it cannot.
That a notebook runs from top to bottom is shown with \texttt{make notebook-\allowbreak{}run}.},
  ai = {Information seeking, Alternative generation, Alternative assessment, Recommendation, Solution generation},
  response = {Accepted},
  assessment = {AI reproduced the crash, measured the exit code and tested every rule on stripped and unstripped notebooks.
It laid out the options and Lukas chose.
Later AI reviews found defects in the wrapper's tests and exit codes, which were fixed before merging.
The notebook that AI drafted failed the cell-length rule and was restructured; the threshold stayed.},
  aievidence = {Claude Code sessions of 2026-10-01 and of 2026-10-05 (review of PR \#67).},
  evidence = {\href{https://github.com/mlops-2627q1-mds-upc/MLOPS_Recommenditos/blob/main/docs/docs/notebooks.md\#pynblint-rules}{Notebooks}, \href{https://github.com/mlops-2627q1-mds-upc/MLOPS_Recommenditos/blob/main/tools/notebook_lint.py}{\texttt{notebook\_\allowbreak{}lint.\allowbreak{}py}}, \href{https://github.com/mlops-2627q1-mds-upc/MLOPS_Recommenditos/blob/main/tools/pynblint-env/pyproject.toml}{\texttt{tools/\allowbreak{}pynblint-\allowbreak{}env/\allowbreak{}}}, \href{https://github.com/mlops-2627q1-mds-upc/MLOPS_Recommenditos/pull/67}{PR \#67}.},
